reason: The text extensively emphasizes hierarchical structures through its narrative focus on royal authority, military command chains, and official ranks. It describes multiple levels of hierarchy: Kings (Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar, Jehoiachin) and their absolute authority; military officers (שְׂרֵי הַחֲיָלִים - captains) and commanders; priestly hierarchy (כֹּהֵן הָרֹאשׁ - chief priest, כֹּהֵן מִשְׁנֶה - second priest); and appointed governmental officials (Gedaliah as governor, the captain of the guard Nebuzaradan, various scribes and officials). The narrative structure itself reinforces that power flows through these hierarchical channels - the king's decisions determine the fate of nations, officials execute orders, and succession of authority is carefully documented.
